purpose: Compare one additional IR-off RAW10 frame using the probe's normal auto-exposure request against the earlier Windows-init manual exposure capture.

conversion.visualInspection: The percentile-stretched frame is brighter than the earlier manual 20 ms / ISO 250 frame, but still appears as mostly fine grain; no eye or useful scene detail is identifiable.

sameSessionExtraRequest.event: A RAW10_INSPECT request also appeared in the same app-session log during teardown; it did not save pixels.

comparison.assessment: Auto-exposure raised the RAW10 level substantially, but no iris detail appeared. AE sensitivity exceeded the advertised maximum, so the brighter values do not establish valid sensor operation or Windows-equivalent exposure. The data still cannot settle native sensor orientation or Windows normalization.

limitations: This was a diffuse non-person IR-off capture; no eye was imaged.
The converter's orientation inputs change split axis/order only and do not rotate pixels.
Image quality, segmentation, matching, enrollment and Android unlock remain unproven.
publication: local only; no commit, push, or PR
